name: Question 1
problem:
Given that $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)$ and

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy),\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{x}{y},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y)$ where all partial derivatives of $f$ exist.
worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)$ is defined only when $xy>0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}={(x,y)\,:\,xy>0}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function ${f}_{x}(x,y)=1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)$ is defined only when $xy>0.$ So, the domain of ${f}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{f}_{x}}={(x,y)\,:\,xy>0}.
$$

- The function ${f}_{y}(x,y)=\frac{x}{y}$ is defined only when $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}={(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partials of $f$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & ={(x,y)\,:\,xy>0}\cap {(x,y)\,:\,xy>0}\cap {(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0} \\  & ={(x,y)\,:\,xy>0}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that f(x,y)=xln⁡(xy) and ∂f∂x=1+ln⁡(xy),∂f∂y=xy, find the set of values (x,y) where all partial derivatives of f exist.

a
{(x,y):y≠0}
b
{(x,y):xy<0}
c
{(x,y):y>0}
d
{(x,y):xy>0}
e
{(x,y):xy≥0}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that f(x,y)=xln⁡(xy) is defined only when xy>0. So, the domain of f is Df={(x,y):xy>0}.

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

  • The function fx(x,y)=1+ln⁡(xy) is defined only when xy>0. So, the domain of fx is Dfx={(x,y):xy>0}.

  • The function fy(x,y)=xy is defined only when y≠0. So, the domain of fy is Dfy={(x,y):y≠0}.

Finally, we conclude that the partials of f exist on the set

Df∩Dfx∩Dfy={(x,y):xy>0}∩{(x,y):xy>0}∩{(x,y):y≠0}={(x,y):xy>0}.
